data.name: Baalaaji
data.gender_notes: Baalaaji is used as a male name in Hindu naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Baalaaji is a Sanskrit name derived from the term 'Bala' meaning 'young one' and 'Ishvara' meaning 'Lord'. In Hindu mythology, Baalaaji is often depicted as the young form of Lord Shiva, the protector of the Universe. The name Baalaaji carries the meaning “Lord of Cows, Young One” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Sanskrit tradition and is also used in Hindi, Sanskrit, Marathi. Parents who choose Baalaaji usually hope their child will grow to embody lord of cows, young one and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: Symbolizes youth, energy, and divine protection.
data.etymology: Baalaaji belongs to the Sanskrit linguistic tradition and is used in Hindu naming. Its recorded meaning is “Lord of Cows, Young One.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Baalaaji total 1, giving a life-path number of 1. Number 1 is linked with Sun and with the qualities of leadership, independence and initiative.

data.cultural_impact: Baalaaji holds a significant cultural impact within the Hindu community, especially among devotees of Lord Shiva. This name embodies the youthful, playful, and protective nature of Lord Shiva. In various temples and shrines dedicated to Lord Shiva, Baalaaji is often revered as a nurturing deity who watches over his devotees, providing them with strength, protection, and joy.
data.spiritual_significance: From a spiritual perspective, the name Baalaaji signifies the compassionate and caring nature of Lord Shiva. It reminds us that even the Supreme God, in His infinite grace, is ever youthful and able to fill our lives with joy and wonder. Additionally, the name instills a sense of trust and protection, evoking a childlike faith in the Lord's abilities to guard us and nurture our souls. Thus, Baalaaji represents the ever-present, loving, and caring aspect of the Divine in our lives.
data.spiritual_symbolism: Baalaaji: The Divine Child, representing innocence, joy, and protection. Symbolizes the nurturing and loving aspect of the Supreme Being, guiding us through childhood and into adulthood.
